summary: This class defines a decorated cookie that builds on the general Cookie class: it inherits the flavor field and adds its own description mentioning sprinkles and icing.

lines.text: The extends keyword sets up the parent/child relationship: DecoratedCookie is a Cookie and automatically receives everything Cookie already provides, so nothing about flavor has to be written twice.

Instead of storing the flavor itself, the subclass hands the value up to the Cookie constructor, which is the pre-bundled starter kit the parent already prepared. Every subclass constructor reaches the parent's constructor this way before adding anything of its own.

This annotation states the intent that describe() is replacing the parent's version, and the compiler will complain if the signature does not actually match one in Cookie — a cheap way to catch a typo in a method name.

lines.code: return "This " + getFlavor() + " cookie is decorated with sprinkles and icing!";
lines.text: The flavor field belongs to Cookie and is private, so the subclass reads it through the inherited getFlavor() method rather than touching the field directly.
